title: Cooling-Off Periods When Buying Property: A State-by-State Guide
excerpt: Cooling-off rights vary dramatically across Australia — here's exactly what protection you have after signing a contract in each state.
body:
Signing a property contract is one of the biggest financial commitments you'll ever make. But what if you change your mind the next day? In Australia, your options depend almost entirely on which state or territory you're buying in — the rules are fragmented, and the consequences of misunderstanding them can cost you thousands.

## What Is a Cooling-Off Period?

A cooling-off period gives a buyer the legal right to withdraw from a signed contract within a set number of business days, usually by paying a small penalty. It exists to protect buyers who feel pressured at auction, who signed before completing due diligence, or who simply had second thoughts.

The critical point: cooling-off periods in Australian residential property are **not uniform**. Each state and territory sets its own rules — some are generous, some are almost useless in practice.

## State-by-State Breakdown

| State/Territory | Cooling-Off Period | Penalty to Exit | Applies After Auction? |
|---|---|---|---|
| NSW | 5 business days | 0.25% of purchase price | No |
| VIC | 3 business days | $100 or 0.2% (whichever is more) | No |
| QLD | 5 business days | 0.25% of purchase price | No |
| SA | 2 business days | $100 flat fee | No |
| WA | None by default | N/A | N/A |
| TAS | None by default | N/A | N/A |
| ACT | 5 business days | 0.25% of purchase price | No |
| NT | 4 business days | 0.25% of purchase price | No |

*Business days, not calendar days, are what count. Always confirm the exact calculation with your solicitor.*

## The Auction Exception — Everywhere

Across every state, **properties purchased at auction have no cooling-off period**. When the hammer falls, you're legally bound. This applies whether you bid in person, by phone, or by proxy. If you later discover a pest problem or change your finances, you cannot walk away without serious legal and financial consequences.

This is why pre-auction building and pest inspections, and pre-auction finance pre-approval, are so important — they're your only safety net.

## Western Australia and Tasmania: Buyer Beware

WA and Tasmania stand out because they have **no statutory cooling-off period** for residential property. Once you sign, you're committed. Buyers in these states rely almost entirely on special conditions written into the contract — such as a finance clause or a building inspection clause — to provide an exit if things go wrong. These need to be drafted carefully by your solicitor before you sign, not after.

## How to Activate a Cooling-Off Period

If you decide to exit during the cooling-off window, the process typically involves:

- Written notice to the vendor or their agent (a signed letter or email)
- The notice must be received before 5 pm on the final business day of the period
- Payment of the applicable penalty, deducted from your deposit
- Return of the remaining deposit, usually within 14 days

Don't assume a phone call is sufficient. Get your solicitor to send the notice formally.

## What Won't Protect You

A few common misconceptions:

- **Verbal agreements** — if you haven't signed, there's nothing to cool off from, but also nothing binding the vendor.
- **Off-the-plan purchases** — these sometimes have extended cooling-off rights under separate legislation, but the standard periods above don't automatically apply.
- **Signing 'subject to finance'** — a finance clause is not the same as a cooling-off period. Finance clauses have their own conditions, timeframes, and dispute risks.

## Practical Steps Before You Sign

- Engage a property solicitor or conveyancer **before** making an offer, not after.
- Always ask what state the property is in and confirm the exact cooling-off rules with your legal representative.
- If buying in WA or Tasmania, negotiate protective special conditions into every contract.
- Never attend an auction without finance pre-approval and completed inspections — there is no exit once bidding closes.
- In states with cooling-off rights, use the period to finalise your building inspection and confirm your loan approval, not to start them.

## Actionable Takeaway

Before you sign any property contract, ask your solicitor two questions: "What is my cooling-off period in this state?" and "What conditions in this contract give me an exit if inspections or finance fall through?" The answers will shape exactly how much risk you're carrying the moment you pick up a pen.
